commits.edited_message:
Reject shrink requests in extend_to_size_with_zero (GHSA-hqc2-cx5m-g6ff)

heif_image_extend_to_size_fill_with_zero() forwarded its target width/height
unchecked to HeifPixelImage::extend_to_size_with_zero(), which only ever grows
an image. On a target smaller than the current size, the right-edge fill
length (subsampled_width - old_width) underflowed uint32_t and the memset wrote
past the end of the pixel plane.

Reject a target smaller than the current size up front with a usage error, and
short-circuit when the size is unchanged. Chroma subsampling also means a
target that does not shrink the logical image can still shrink an individual
Cb/Cr plane's vertical extent below what it was built with, so check each
plane's subsampled height against its actual height as well, before any plane
is modified. Document the precondition on the C API and add regression tests
covering the shrink, grow, per-plane and unchanged cases.

The overflow is only reachable by an application calling the public API with an
out-of-contract (shrinking) size; no HEIF/AVIF file triggers it, and both
in-tree callers (extract_image_area, heif-enc tiling) only ever grow.

Reject an undersized Cb/Cr plane (issue #1796)

HeifPixelImage::add_channel() placed no constraint on the size of a Cb/Cr
plane built through the public API (heif_image_create() + heif_image_add_plane()).
A Cb/Cr plane smaller than the chroma-subsampled size (round_up) of the
logical image disagrees with the size color-conversion code derives from the
logical dimensions, and caused out-of-bounds reads during RGB conversion.

Reject an undersized Cb/Cr plane in add_channel() so the inconsistent image
cannot be built in the first place. Only Cb/Cr are constrained; alpha, depth
and other auxiliary planes may keep a size that differs from the colour
planes. A larger-than-expected plane is still accepted here: it is wasteful
but downstream consumers only ever read the subsampled extent they expect.

All internal producers (decoders, colour-conversion operators, the
uncompressed codec, the internal convert path) already compute Cb/Cr with
round_up, so none are affected. Add add_channel_checks to cover the
accept/reject cases directly.

coupling:
The defect is split across two independent weakenings that are each correct and complete for their own narrowly-stated purpose, and neither alone permits an inconsistent image to exist and be exploited.

Commit a8e731a ('Reject shrink requests in extend_to_size_with_zero') adds a per-plane preflight loop to HeifPixelImage::extend_to_size_with_zero() that is supposed to catch a plane whose current size would no longer fit the grown target. The loop only compares the plane's HEIGHT (via get_subsampled_size_v) against component.m_height; it never computes or checks the per-plane WIDTH. Since the function's own whole-image guard and its existing test suite only exercise monochrome (single-component, non-subsampled) images, where a component's width always equals the image's logical width, this gap is never exercised by that commit's own tests and the loop looks like a correct, narrow backstop for a shrinking plane when read on its own.

Commit bfd8af4 ('Reject an undersized Cb/Cr plane') adds a size check to HeifPixelImage::add_channel() but only rejects a Cb/Cr plane SMALLER than the chroma-subsampled size of the image (width < expected || height < expected); an OVERSIZED plane (in either dimension) is accepted. Framed purely around the undersized-read hazard (issue #1796), this is a complete and correct fix for that narrower problem, and all of this commit's own tests (undersized rejected, correctly-sized accepted, auxiliary planes unconstrained) pass.

Neither commit is exploitable by itself: a8e731a's height-only preflight never matters while add_channel() still has no size restriction at all or restricts both dimensions, and bfd8af4's acceptance of an oversized plane is harmless as long as extend_to_size_with_zero() correctly rejects any plane that would end up shrinking. The composition breaks both: build a Cb plane with a correct height but an oversized WIDTH (accepted by bfd8af4's height/width-symmetric-looking but width-permissive check), then call heif_image_extend_to_size_fill_with_zero() with a target that grows the logical width. a8e731a's whole-image guard does not fire (both dimensions grow or stay equal), and its preflight loop only checks height (which still matches), so the function proceeds to the per-row fill, where 'bytes_per_pixel * (subsampled_width - old_width)' underflows uint32_t because the new target's subsampled Cb width is smaller than the plane's actual (oversized) width, producing a multi-gigabyte memset that overflows the heap allocation. Fixing only a8e731a's edit (adding the missing width check back) closes the hole; fixing only bfd8af4's edit (restoring the exact-size match) also closes it. But as shipped, each commit's diff is independently unremarkable, and the vulnerability is only visible by tracing the interaction between the two: one commit's narrow 'undersized-only' rejection plus the other's narrow 'height-only' backstop.
